SEO review (2026-11-27): the meta description promised two easy jazz shapes but the page calls the 9 chord blues/funk, use: Can't play F or B yet? Fmaj7, B7, four-string minor chords, triads and two no-barre shapes, with audio for each. Quick record shouldn't be an H2. The H2 '7. A maj7 on the low E' breaks across elements: make it one plain text heading. B♭, Fm and Gm are barely in the body: cover them. Chord-box labels clutter the text Google reads: aria-hidden on the box labels plus one short text description per chord ('Fmaj7: x-x-3-2-1-0'). Article schema with author and dateModified.
Let's add min7 jazz drop 3 chord
calculator: npm run -s theory -- scale C major (Fmaj7 = F A C E; x x 3 2 1 0 puts E on the open high e)
npm run -s theory -- triads C --group 321 --chords IV --frets 0-3 (F: 2-1-1, A C F)
npm run -s theory -- triads E --group 321 --chords V --frets 2-5 (B: 4-4-2, B D♯ F♯)
Chord boxes checked by chord-shapes' shapeFromFrets against each chord's notes: C9 x 3 2 3 3 x = C E B♭ D; Fmaj7 1 x 2 2 1 x = F E A C; B7 open from the chord library
npm run -s theory -- triads C --group 432 --chords IV,V --frets 0-5 (F 3-2-1 F A C, G 5-4-3 G B D: the Fmaj7 shape's fretted notes, slid two frets)
npm run -s theory -- box B minor A (Bm x-2-4-4-3-2; the four-string one x x 4 4 3 2 = F♯ B D F♯, 5 R ♭3 5)
npm run -s theory -- positions C minor pentatonic (position 4, frets 3-6: E 3 G, 6 B♭; A 3 C, 6 E♭; under Cm x x 5 5 4 3)
The chord finder's shapes (alternatives.ts) are checked by alternatives.test.ts against shapeFromFrets for all 24 major and minor chords; triads come from chordKit's triadVoicings
C7 x 3 2 3 1 x = C E B♭ C (B7 x 2 1 2 0 2 one fret up, the open B string pressed at the 1st fret, high e left out), checked by shapeFromFrets
npm run -s theory -- triads A --group 432 --chords I --frets 4-8 (A 7-6-5: the F triad slid four frets)

D shape moved: E x x 2 4 5 4, F♯ x x 4 6 7 6; Dm shape moved: Em x x 2 4 5 3, F♯m x x 4 6 7 5; Fmaj7 1 x 2 2 1 x fingered 1 x 3 4 2 x, Gmaj7 and Amaj7 two and four frets up; all checked by shapeFromFrets
The fill under Cm (x x 5 5 4 3), top four strings only, C minor pentatonic position 4 without the 5: F (B 6), E♭ (B 4), C (G 5); then B♭ (G 3), F (D 3), B♭ (G 3), C (G 5). Bass: C (A 3)

npm run -s theory -- triads Bb --group 321 --chords I (B♭ 3-3-1: the B triad 4-4-2 one fret down); triads F minor and G minor --group 321,432 (Fm 3-5-6-4 = F C F A♭ and Gm 5-7-8-6 = G D G B♭: the Dm shape x x 0 2 3 1 three and five frets up), checked by shapeFromFrets

npm run -s theory -- scale Eb major / F major / G major (ii = Fm7: F A♭ C E♭, Gm7: G B♭ D F, Am7: A C E G); the drop 3 m7 on the low E, R x ♭7 ♭3 5: Fm7 1 x 1 1 1 x, Gm7 3 x 3 3 3 x, Am7 5 x 5 5 5 x, fingering 1 x 2 3 4 x
open: The four-string minor is now the open Am shape moved up (root on the A string, low E and A muted), as the author asked on review; the author's "finger 345" read as fingers 2, 3 and 4 counting the thumb as 1, with the first finger on the high e.
Search volume for the query not checked yet.

"mute the lowest string" read as the open high e (the string nearest the floor): Fmaj7 x x 3 2 1 0 without it is F x x 3 2 1 x. The "Move it" wording follows the course's Move it: G minor (/course/5/move-it): the open strings were doing work.
No "Make it your own" section, against VOICE.md: the author asked for a Summary in its place. No "Practice until" lines: the author finds them wrong in an article.
"index on top string" for the low-E Fmaj7 read as the low E string (the one at the top as you hold the guitar).
